primary_goal: Build practical, increasingly independent European Portuguese communication for everyday life in Portugal.
design_principles: Situation-first: define the communicative outcome before selecting vocabulary and grammar.
Teach question words and connectors from the first days and revisit them throughout the curriculum.
Prioritize speaking and interaction over isolated memorization.
Use European Portuguese; informal tu with peers and polite service requests when appropriate.
Include past events, current states, and near-future plans in the first 30 days.
Each lesson progresses from noticing to transformations, guided production, open production, and transfer.
Friend chat remains learner-led; lesson completion must not force rigid conversation outside Practice.
Targeted, exposed, produced, and mastered are different states.
UI and rendering decisions are out of scope for these JSON content files.
Classify vocabulary by frequency, communicative utility, and sentence-building value; do not force all 1000 source words into 90 days.
Teach a small, immediately usable grammar pattern from Day 1; grammar is a speaking tool, not a delayed theory unit.
Every sentence example must be connected to the lesson's vocabulary and real-life scenario.
High-priority words recur in later contexts; low-priority words are deferred rather than used to fill quotas.

content_mapping.question_words: question words deliberately taught or reused

vocabulary_policy.source: 1000 Palavras Mais Comuns.md, supplemented by practical European Portuguese communication needs.
vocabulary_policy.scope_note: The source list is a reference inventory, not a quota. The 90-day course intentionally teaches a selected subset; lower-priority words remain for post-day-90 extension.

classification.name: Core function and survival communication
classification.rule: Teach from Day 1: pronouns, question words, negation, basic verbs, core connectors, repair phrases and sentence-building tools.

classification.name: High-frequency everyday language
classification.rule: Introduce early when it supports many contexts: common verbs, time, places, requests, daily needs.

classification.name: Contextual everyday vocabulary
classification.rule: Introduce when the scenario makes the word useful and the learner has enough structure to use it.

classification.name: Specialized or lower-priority vocabulary
classification.rule: Defer until later lessons or a post-90-day extension unless needed for an important real-life scenario.

classification.name: Lowest-priority / abstract vocabulary
classification.rule: Do not add just to fill lesson space; prioritize only when there is a clear communicative reason.

vocabulary_policy.mastery_note: Lesson count and word count are not targets. Prioritize usable spoken language, spaced retrieval, and accurate contextual sentence production.

progression.goal: Start conversations, ask questions, connect ideas, and manage everyday needs.
Tell experiences, explain problems, interact with services, and express opinions.
Handle longer, flexible conversations, solve problems, tell stories, and confirm understanding.

question_word_policy.rule: Teach complete question patterns and follow-up behavior, not translations alone.
